class_decision_verbatim.question: WARRANT-rival entries whose rejected alternative keeps the row's onset and extends the row forward, the entry sitting on the verse after the row's last verse (17 items + the qualifier part of S4-085).
class_decision_verbatim.reading_A_lane_A: the seam pair is the seam the merge would dissolve (row's last verse / entry's first verse) with :near on the entry's verse - 'the first absorbed verse is the rival's near face'; lane A labels this INFERRED convention; lane B lists it as option (a) 'contested own seam, positional faces'.
class_decision_verbatim.reading_B_lane_B: clause 6 v2 defines a rival's :near as 'the candidate onset verse for a rival' and #e15 defines a rival as 'an interior seam. Near face = the candidate onset verse; far face = the verse before it'; a forward merge proposes no onset at the entry's verse (the row does) and no interior seam; own_seam_faces makes that verse the FAR face of the row's close seam while the member's rival check forces :near on the later verse of any pair; the ruling's one worked merge rival (17.10/17.11) anchors on the merged unit's own first verse, which for a forward merge is the row's first verse (option (b), re-anchoring, outside qualify/re-token/re-face/re-gloss); option (c) is a close-shaped rival grammar in the member.
class_decision_verbatim.why_not_decided_here: Clause 6 v2 and #e15 as written define a rival face only through a candidate onset verse on an interior seam; the worked example (a backward merge, the rival unit's own first verse before the row's onset) does not reach a forward merge; own_seam_faces gives the same verse the opposite polarity. Reading A adds a meaning the clause does not give ('first absorbed verse = near'); reading B's options re-anchor entries or change the member. Each is a vocabulary ruling, so per the adjudication brief the class goes to #e16 with both readings and every affected entry, and the rivals stay unqualified as recorded STOPs. That the role_tokens member's phase flip waits is not weighed.

the_finding_that_changes_the_scope.what: all three לכן verses are the FIRST verse of their row and the preceding row ends at the verse immediately before (P03-011 ends 17:18, P04-002 ends 20:29, P09-010 ends 39:24). These are cuts the corpus made.
the_finding_that_changes_the_scope.consequence: #e15 routed the class expecting it to settle three grades. If the turn is NOT a licensed onset, three shipped seams rest on an unlicensed onset, which is a SPAN question in three places. Chs 17, 20-21 and 38-39 are all named §7 regions, so those seams would go to the OW-6b(b) second Fable review with this table as input - the same disposition the ch-18 tiling question received.
the_finding_that_changes_the_scope.why_i_am_not_deciding_it: the precedents point one way - #e15 held that two titles for one audience inside one speech do not satisfy limb (a), and #e13 resolved that a mark-only close does not satisfy limb (b) - but a class ruling that reaches three spans is a controlling-agent decision, not an orchestrator's inference.
the_finding_that_changes_the_scope.tier: seam positions and adjacent rows MEASURED; the span consequence INFERRED from the ruling's limbs
